spec.baseline: fixed: full clock when busy, 18 C supply, design flow
spec.configuration: 8 accelerators on one liquid loop; dry cooler + trim chiller; see parameter registry
controlled_variables: thermal target 80 C / hardware throttle 85 C
spec.data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
spec.evaluation_criteria: Primary: paired relative difference in E_per_success_kJ. A difference is 'meaningful' only if the whole 95% CI lies beyond 1%. Quality guard: success_rate and SLO violations must not worsen relative to the comparator. Thermal guard: zero chip-seconds throttled.
spec.hypothesis: H1: joint uses less energy per successful task than independent in at least 4 of 6 scenarios (paired 95% CI entirely below 0), without more SLO violations or thermal-limit exceedances. H2: every optimising policy uses less energy per successful task than fixed in every scenario.
spec.known_limitations: Synthetic workload (class F); controller has a perfect model of the plant; quasi-steady plant without loop thermal mass; single node; constant ambient per scenario.
spec.null_hypothesis: Joint and independent do not differ (CI includes 0) or differ by less than the practical threshold.
spec.research_question: How much facility energy per successful task does each control strategy save relative to a fixed conventional policy, and does joint compute-cooling optimisation save more than energy-aware compute and cooling controllers running independently?
spec.statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
spec.title: Policy benchmark: fixed vs compute-only vs cooling-only vs independent vs joint

spec.baseline: default variant; fixed policy within each variant
controlled_variables: scenario S1_moderate shortened to a 2 h arrival window (one load cycle)
spec.data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
spec.evaluation_criteria: For each variant: paired relative difference joint vs independent and joint vs fixed with 95% CI (n=3 seeds, so CIs are wide; used for ranking, not confirmation). Rank parameters by the swing (high minus low) of the mean difference.
spec.hypothesis: The sign of (joint - independent) energy per successful task is non-positive for every one-at-a-time variation; its magnitude is most sensitive to the leakage parameters (kappa_leak, p_leak_ref). The joint-vs-fixed saving is most sensitive to the V-f curve (v_min_ratio) and memory-boundness (beta_memory).
independent_variables: one parameter at its low or high bound (25 parameters x 2)
spec.known_limitations: One-at-a-time design misses interactions; only 3 seeds per cell; ranges are judgement calls recorded in the registry.
spec.null_hypothesis: Some variation reverses the sign of joint - independent, or other parameters dominate.
spec.research_question: Which uncertain (class E/F) assumptions materially change the conclusions of E001 for joint vs independent and joint vs fixed?
spec.statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
spec.title: One-at-a-time sensitivity of policy comparisons to uncertain assumptions

spec.baseline: routing off (large model only) under the same policy
spec.configuration: All routing parameters are hypothetical (class F); see registry
controlled_variables: task arrivals and outcome random numbers per seed
spec.data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
spec.evaluation_criteria: Paired relative difference of each routing variant vs routing_off within policy; compare with analytic work ratio from workload.routing_expectations().
spec.hypothesis: With a perfect verifier the cascade reduces energy per successful task if and only if (small cost + verifier cost) < E[p_small] = 0.672; the realised fractional energy saving is smaller than the fractional work saving because idle, static, conversion and cooling energy do not scale with work. A verifier with false accepts lowers task success.
independent_variables: routing on/off and small-model cost ratio
spec.known_limitations: Quality model is a Bernoulli placeholder, not a measured model evaluation; verifier cost and accuracy are assumed; no batching effects.
spec.null_hypothesis: Energy saving tracks work saving one-to-one, or the break-even point differs from analytic.
spec.research_question: Does a verified small-model cascade reduce facility energy per successful task, and how does the realised energy saving compare with the analytic saving in computational work?
spec.statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
spec.title: Model-routing cascade with verification: realised energy vs analytic work savings

spec.baseline: same true plant with a correct twin
spec.configuration: Mismatch applied only to the controller's model config (model_param_overrides).
spec.data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
spec.evaluation_criteria: Within each truth case: joint vs independent paired difference with correct vs wrong twin; count chip-seconds over target.
spec.hypothesis: When the twin underestimates leakage or overestimates cold-plate performance, the joint controller exceeds the 80 C thermal target for some chip-seconds and loses part or all of its advantage over independent control; hardware protection still bounds temperature.
independent_variables: twin-vs-truth mismatch (3 cases, each with a matched-truth reference)
spec.known_limitations: Mismatches are single-parameter-group and static; real drift is gradual and correlated.
spec.null_hypothesis: Joint retains its advantage and meets the thermal target under every mismatch.
spec.research_question: How much of the joint controller's advantage survives when its digital twin is wrong, and do thermal limits still hold?
spec.statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
spec.title: Robustness of model-based control to digital-twin mismatch

spec.baseline: quasi-steady plant (identical to E001) within each policy; independent within each plant
spec.configuration: Loop mass and ramp values are class F placeholders (CDU tank + piping), not measurements.
spec.data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
dependent_variables: E_loop_storage_kWh (must stay below 0.5% of grid energy)
spec.disclosure: v1 (E006-20261026T184900-8dd0d3) ran with a cold start: the joint controller's first decision, made at zero demand, chose 12 C, and the dynamic plant used that setpoint as the initial tank temperature. The joint runs then drew down that stored coldness (up to 4.9 kWh of heat absorbed and never rejected), which overstated joint's advantage under dynamic plants. Found by examining v1's energy breakdown. v2 adds warm_start to every variant so each policy starts in its own steady state; hypotheses are unchanged. v1 results were seen before v2 was registered. Before v1, only unit tests ran on the dynamic plant.
spec.evaluation_criteria: Paired relative differences with 95% t-CI; practical threshold 1%. H2/H4 judged on seed means of chip-seconds above target.
spec.hypothesis: H1: joint uses less energy per successful task than independent (paired 95% CI below 0) in all 3 scenarios under both dynamic plants. H2: under the slow plant (150 kg, 0.25 K/min) joint records chip-seconds above the 80 C target in at least one scenario, because it plans against a steady state the plant cannot reach quickly. H3: the fixed policy's energy changes by less than 0.5% between quasi-steady and dynamic plants (its setpoint never moves). H4: joint_robust records no more chip-seconds above target than joint in every scenario and plant.
independent_variables: plant model (quasi-steady, 40 kg + 1 K/min, 150 kg + 0.25 K/min)
spec.known_limitations: Single well-mixed tank; no pipe transport delay; ramp limit is symmetric; controllers still plan with a steady-state twin.
spec.null_hypothesis: The joint advantage disappears (CI includes 0) under a dynamic plant, and loop dynamics do not affect thermal safety.
spec.research_question: Does the joint controller's advantage over independent control, and its thermal safety, survive when the coolant loop has thermal mass and the plant cannot move its outlet temperature instantly?
spec.statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
spec.title: Joint control under a dynamic coolant loop (thermal mass + setpoint ramp limits)

spec.data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
spec.disclosure: Before registration one exploratory run (S1, seed 4, dt 1 s) showed action changes falling from 102 to 89 at a 5% threshold, with all switching in clocks and flow and none in supply temperature. H1 was written after seeing that run. No dt comparison with suppression was run.
spec.evaluation_criteria: H1 on seed-mean action changes; H2 on max over seeds of |E(dt=1)/E(dt=0.5) - 1| within each threshold; H3 paired CI of energy per successful task.
spec.hypothesis: H1: thresholds up to 5% cut the number of action changes by less than 25%, because most switching tracks demand rather than chatters. H2: at a 2% threshold the worst per-seed change in grid energy between dt = 1 s and dt = 0.5 s falls below 0.5% in both scenarios. H3: a 2% threshold costs at most 0.3% energy per successful task versus no threshold.
spec.known_limitations: Threshold acts on predicted, not measured, savings.
spec.null_hypothesis: Suppression neither reduces time-step sensitivity nor is cheap.
spec.research_question: Can a switching threshold make the joint controller's results insensitive to the simulation time step (E004 failed at 0.52%) without costing energy?
spec.statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
spec.title: Move suppression for the joint controller: switching, energy cost, and time-step sensitivity

spec.baseline: independent within each case; joint within each case
spec.configuration: Mismatch cases as E005, plus the registry default.
spec.data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
spec.disclosure: Before registration a unit test ran S3_hot (1 h, seed 0) with the leakage mismatch and showed joint_robust with fewer than half of joint's chip-seconds above target.
spec.evaluation_criteria: Paired relative differences with 95% t-CI; practical threshold 1%; chip-second counts as seed means.
spec.hypothesis: H1: in every mismatch case where joint exceeded the 80 C target, joint_robust has zero chip-seconds throttled and at least 80% fewer chip-seconds above target than joint. H2: joint_robust uses no more energy per successful task than independent (paired 95% CI upper bound <= 0) in every case. H3: with a correct twin (default and *_twin_correct variants), joint_robust is within +/-0.5% of joint on energy per successful task.
spec.known_limitations: The correction only tightens the temperature target; it does not re-estimate leakage, so energy predictions stay biased.
spec.null_hypothesis: The correction does not remove overheating, or it removes it only by giving up the energy advantage.
spec.research_question: Does feeding measured junction temperatures back into the joint controller (one-sided offset-free correction) restore thermal safety under twin mismatch without giving up its energy advantage?
spec.statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
spec.title: Self-correcting joint control under digital-twin mismatch

spec.configuration: E001 design with calibrated overrides {'beta_compute': 0.983, 'beta_memory': 0.0}; every other parameter at its registry value.
controlled_variables: thermal target 80 C / hardware throttle 85 C
spec.data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
dependent_variables: seed-paired change vs E001 in compute_only/fixed and joint/independent relative energy per successful task
spec.disclosure: The calibration values were known when these hypotheses were written; E001C results were not. Acceptance rules R1-R3 were set after seeing the first desktop fit summary and before examining raw telemetry. Before registration, a forensic check re-ran 24 seed-0 E001 cells with the first (rejected) fit's values to identify orphaned time-series files; only their time series were compared, not their outcomes. No runs with the accepted values preceded registration.
spec.evaluation_criteria: As E001 for H1-H2 (paired 95% t-CI, practical threshold 1%). HC1-HC3: for each scenario and seed, d = (a/b - 1) in E001C minus (a/b - 1) in E001 on E_per_success_kJ, with a/b = compute_only/fixed (HC1, HC2) or joint/independent (HC3); 95% t-CI over the 10 seeds.
spec.hypothesis: Inherited from E001 and re-tested: H1: joint uses less energy per successful task than independent in at least 4 of 6 scenarios (paired 95% CI entirely below 0), without more SLO violations or thermal-limit exceedances. H2: every optimising policy uses less energy per successful task than fixed in every scenario. New: HC1: compute_only saves more energy per successful task relative to fixed in E001C than in E001, in all 6 scenarios (seed-paired change in relative saving, 95% CI entirely below 0), because with beta_memory = 0 memory-bound phases lose no throughput when the clock drops. HC2: that change is largest in S5_memory_heavy. HC3: joint's advantage over independent changes by less than 0.5 percentage points (95% CI of the seed-paired change within +/-0.5 pp) in at least 5 of 6 scenarios, because both policies use the same DVFS model.
spec.inherits: E001 (same design, seeds and workloads; only the calibrated parameters differ)
spec.known_limitations: Only clock sensitivity is calibrated. v_min_ratio, kappa_leak and p_leak_ref stay registry placeholders: their fits were rejected (docs/10). The measured power-vs-clock shape is not represented: with registry defaults the simulator misstates normalised power by up to 0.09 and energy per unit of work by up to 0.09 of the top-clock value. beta_memory = 0 comes from a pure streaming kernel and is a bound for LLM decode, not a measurement of it. One consumer GPU.
spec.null_hypothesis: Calibrating clock sensitivity changes neither the savings from DVFS nor the policy ranking.
spec.research_question: Do the Phase 1 conclusions survive when the two parameters measured on real hardware (clock sensitivity of compute-bound and memory-bound work) replace the placeholders?
spec.statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
spec.title: Policy benchmark with measured clock sensitivity (M001: RTX 5070)

assumptions.name: water_cp
assumptions.source: Liquid water near 25 C. NIST WebBook (Shomate eq.) gives ~4.184 J/(g K) at 25 C and ~4.178 at 40-45 C; see reference_values.md

assumptions.name: water_rho
assumptions.source: Density of liquid water near 25 C

assumptions.name: k_boltzmann
assumptions.source: SI exact value (NIST); see reference_values.md

assumptions.name: n_accel
assumptions.source: Size of simulated cluster (one 8-accelerator node)

assumptions.name: p_dyn_max
assumptions.source: Dynamic power at s=1, V=Vmax, activity=1. Total ~620 W at s=1 and 60 C, comparable to the 'up to 700 W' max TDP NVIDIA lists for H100 SXM (class D, reference_values.md). Not a model of any product

assumptions.name: p_leak_ref
assumptions.source: Leakage at t_leak_ref and Vmax, ~15% of total. Breen et al. 2011 (L26, simulation) put typical chip leakage near 10% with projections up to ~50%; the range brackets both

assumptions.name: t_leak_ref
assumptions.source: Reference junction temperature for leakage

assumptions.name: kappa_leak
assumptions.source: P_leak ~ exp(kappa*(T-Tref)); 0.02/K doubles every ~35 K. Form is an approximation: Price et al. 2015 (L28, measured on a K20 GPU) fit a T^2*exp(-b/T) law instead. Needs refitting on a current GPU (Phase 4)

assumptions.name: p_static_other
assumptions.source: Temperature-independent board power (memory, I/O, fans excluded)

assumptions.name: idle_dyn_frac
assumptions.source: Fraction of full dynamic power drawn when idle (clock tree etc.)

assumptions.name: activity_memory
assumptions.source: Relative switching activity of memory-bound work vs compute-bound work

assumptions.name: s_min
assumptions.source: Lowest normalized clock frequency available (f/fmax)

assumptions.name: v_min_ratio
assumptions.source: Vmin/Vmax at s_min; voltage assumed linear in frequency between s_min and 1

assumptions.name: beta_compute
assumptions.source: Throughput ~ s**beta for compute-bound work (beta=1 is perfectly clock-bound)

assumptions.name: beta_memory
assumptions.source: Throughput ~ s**beta for memory-bound work. Maliakel et al. 2025 (L09, preprint) report LLM decode latency changing <1% across clock settings, i.e. beta near 0, which is BELOW this range; a lower value would make DVFS look even better

assumptions.name: c_th
assumptions.source: Lumped heat capacity of die + package + cold plate

assumptions.name: r_cond
assumptions.source: Conduction resistance junction -> wetted cold-plate surface (die, TIM, lid, base)

assumptions.name: r_conv_ref
assumptions.source: Convective resistance at design flow. For scale: a measured direct-to-chip cold plate (heater rig, not a GPU) showed 7.6-10.4 mK/W total at ~1 kW (reference_values.md, class B)

assumptions.name: n_conv
assumptions.source: R_conv ~ flow**(-n). ~0.8 for turbulent (Dittus-Boelter), lower for developing laminar flow

assumptions.name: t_target
assumptions.source: Junction temperature limit that controllers must respect

assumptions.name: t_throttle
assumptions.source: Independent hardware protection trip point (throttles to s_min regardless of controller)

assumptions.name: throttle_hyst
assumptions.source: Throttle release hysteresis

assumptions.name: flow_design_lpm
assumptions.source: Gives ~8 K coolant rise at ~650 W (Q = m_dot*cp*dT)

assumptions.name: flow_min_factor
assumptions.source: Lowest allowed flow / design flow

assumptions.name: flow_max_factor
assumptions.source: Highest allowed flow / design flow

assumptions.name: dp_ref
assumptions.source: Loop pressure drop at design flow

assumptions.name: m_dp
assumptions.source: dP ~ flow**m. m=1 laminar (Hagen-Poiseuille), ~1.75-2 turbulent (Darcy-Weisbach)

assumptions.name: eta_pump
assumptions.source: Pump wire-to-water efficiency

assumptions.name: t_sup_min
assumptions.source: Lowest supply temperature the plant can deliver

assumptions.name: t_sup_max
assumptions.source: Highest supply temperature allowed; ASHRAE class W45 upper supply limit (reference_values.md)

assumptions.name: eta_ii_chiller
assumptions.source: Chiller second-law efficiency: COP = eta_II * COP_Carnot

assumptions.name: dt_evap
assumptions.source: Evaporator approach (T_evap = T_sup - dt_evap)

assumptions.name: dt_cond
assumptions.source: Condenser approach (T_cond = T_amb + dt_cond)

assumptions.name: dt_drycooler
assumptions.source: Dry-cooler approach to ambient

assumptions.name: fan_ratio
assumptions.source: Heat-rejection fan power per W of heat rejected to ambient

assumptions.name: cop_max
assumptions.source: Numerical cap on chiller COP when lift approaches zero

assumptions.name: eta_conv
assumptions.source: Grid-to-chip power conversion efficiency (UPS, PSU, VRs)

assumptions.name: t_reuse_min
assumptions.source: Return temperature needed for heat to count as reusable

assumptions.name: job_work_mean
assumptions.source: Mean job size in seconds at s=1 (lognormal)

assumptions.name: job_work_sigma
assumptions.source: Lognormal sigma of job size

assumptions.name: frac_memory
assumptions.source: Fraction of jobs that are memory-bound

assumptions.name: slo_base
assumptions.source: Latency SLO = slo_base + slo_factor * nominal work

assumptions.name: slo_factor
assumptions.source: Latency SLO multiplier on nominal work

assumptions.name: u_max
assumptions.source: Max planned utilization (queueing headroom) for optimizing controllers

assumptions.name: frac_easy
assumptions.source: Fraction of tasks a small model can handle

assumptions.name: small_cost_ratio
assumptions.source: Small-model work / large-model work

assumptions.name: verify_cost_ratio
assumptions.source: Verifier work / large-model work

assumptions.name: p_small_easy
assumptions.source: Small-model success probability on easy tasks

assumptions.name: p_small_hard
assumptions.source: Small-model success probability on hard tasks

assumptions.name: p_large
assumptions.source: Large-model success probability

assumptions.name: verifier_false_accept
assumptions.source: P(verifier accepts a wrong small-model answer)

assumptions.name: verifier_false_reject
assumptions.source: P(verifier rejects a correct small-model answer)

assumptions.name: loop_mass_kg
assumptions.source: 0 selects the quasi-steady plant of E001-E005 (no loop thermal mass). E006 uses 40 kg and 150 kg; those values are placeholders (class F) for a CDU tank + piping, not measurements

assumptions.name: warm_start
assumptions.source: 1 = controllers start with the demand estimate and chip-heat estimate of the initial offered load, as if the system had been running, so each policy starts in its own steady state. 0 = cold start with zero demand estimate (E001-E005, E006 v1). Needed with a loop thermal mass: in E006 v1 a cold start let the first (zero-demand) decision set the initial tank temperature, a confound found in analysis

assumptions.name: tsup_ramp_K_per_min
assumptions.source: Max rate at which the plant can move its outlet temperature. 0 = instantaneous (E001-E005). E006 uses 1.0 and 0.25 (class F placeholders)

assumptions.name: fixed_t_sup
assumptions.source: Supply temperature of the fixed (conventional) baseline; within ASHRAE W17/W27-class supply ranges

assumptions.name: fixed_flow
assumptions.source: Flow factor of the fixed baseline policy

assumptions.name: t_assume_compute
assumptions.source: Junction temperature a compute-only controller (no thermal model) assumes

assumptions.name: t_sup_step
assumptions.source: Supply-temperature grid resolution for optimizing controllers

assumptions.name: joint_switch_rel
assumptions.source: Move suppression: the joint controller keeps its previous action unless the new optimum is predicted to use this fraction less grid power (0 = always switch, as in E001-E005)

assumptions.name: joint_bias_gain
assumptions.source: EWMA gain of the joint_robust controller's temperature-bias estimate (measured minus predicted peak junction temperature, clipped at 0); used only by joint_robust

assumptions.name: dt
assumptions.source: Simulation time step

assumptions.name: control_interval
assumptions.source: Controller decision period

assumptions.name: log_interval
assumptions.source: Time-series logging period

assumptions.name: demand_window
assumptions.source: Window for demand estimation (EWMA time constant)

assumptions.name: backlog_clear_s
assumptions.source: Controllers plan to clear current backlog within this time

assumptions.name: drain_max_s
assumptions.source: Max time after last arrival to finish queued work

research_log: Phase 0/1 start. Environment: Linux container, 2 CPU cores, 7.8 GB RAM, no GPU, no EDA tools installed; Python 3.13, NumPy 2.5, SciPy 1.18. Consequence: Phase 4 (hardware telemetry) and RTL work cannot be done here.

Disclosure: before registering E001-E005, a single smoke run (seed 1, S1_moderate, all five policies) was executed to check the code runs. It showed joint ~0.7% below independent and DVFS-driven savings of ~30% vs fixed. The 1% practical-significance threshold and all hypotheses were written after seeing that one run; treat H1 accordingly.

Validation suite: 42 tests passing (analytic RC transient, leakage runaway boundary, coolant/pump hand calcs, Carnot bound, energy closure, reproducibility, twin-vs-sim steady state, hardware protection, dt convergence, routing vs analytic, store immutability and tamper detection).

Registered E004-20261026T180014-01ec84: Numerical convergence in the time step | H: Grid energy and energy per successful task change by less than 0.5% between dt=0.5 s and dt=1 s for both fixed and joint policies.

Registered E001-20261026T180020-09ee19: Policy benchmark: fixed vs compute-only vs cooling-only vs independent vs joint | H: H1: joint uses less energy per successful task than independent in at least 4 of 6 scenarios (paired 95% CI entirely below 0), without more SLO violations or thermal-limit exceedances. H2: every optimising policy uses less energy per successful task than fixed in every scenario.

Registered E003-20261026T180404-1c3acc: Model-routing cascade with verification: realised energy vs analytic work savings | H: With a perfect verifier the cascade reduces energy per successful task if and only if (small cost + verifier cost) < E[p_small] = 0.672; the realised fractional energy saving is smaller than the fractional work saving because idle, static, conversion and cooling energy do not scale with work. A verifier with false accepts lowers task success.
Aborted E003-20261026T180404-1c3acc: stopped: plant bug (negative chiller work) found in E001 v1 analysis; rerun with fixed code (82 unfinished runs marked failed)

BUG FOUND during E001 v1 analysis: in S4_cool, E_chiller_kWh was slightly negative (about -0.001 kWh). Cause: when a controller raises supply temperature above an idle chip's temperature, heat flows from coolant into the chip; the quasi-steady plant booked that as negative chiller work. Fix: plant clamps rejected heat at zero and books the deficit as loop storage (E_loop_storage_kWh, <= 0), energy balance updated. Regression tests added. E001 v1 and E004 v1 are kept in the store unchanged and superseded by v2 runs; E003 v1 aborted mid-run (finished runs kept).

Registered E004-20261026T180548-d4faa6: Numerical convergence in the time step | H: Grid energy and energy per successful task change by less than 0.5% between dt=0.5 s and dt=1 s for both fixed and joint policies.

Registered E001-20261026T180555-756536: Policy benchmark: fixed vs compute-only vs cooling-only vs independent vs joint | H: H1: joint uses less energy per successful task than independent in at least 4 of 6 scenarios (paired 95% CI entirely below 0), without more SLO violations or thermal-limit exceedances. E006 v1 CONFOUND found in analysis: with a cold start, the joint controller's first decision (zero demand) chose 12 C supply and the dynamic plant used that as the initial tank temperature. Joint runs then used up that stored coldness (E_loop_storage up to +4.87 kWh per run in S3 with the 150 kg loop), lowering leakage and fan energy and making joint look 4.8% better than independent; independent started near its own steady state. Fix: warm_start option (controllers start with the initial-load demand and heat estimates, so every policy starts in its own steady state) plus a run warning when loop storage change exceeds 0.5% of grid energy; regression test added; legacy results still reproduce bitwise. E006 v1 is kept and superseded by v2 (warm start in every variant, hypotheses unchanged, v1 results seen before v2 registration). E007 and E008 use the quasi-steady plant (no loop storage) and are unaffected.

Phase 2-4 session summary: E006 v2 (warm start) shows joint beats independent by 0.4-1.5% under dynamic loops (all CIs below 0) and loses thermal margin under loop lag with degraded cooling (131 and 421 chip-s above 80 C, no throttling); self-correcting control does not fix lag (H4 false). E007: move suppression changes switching by 16-25% at 5%, costs 0.4-0.5% energy there, and does not change time-step sensitivity (already <0.5% on 4 h runs). E008: temperature-feedback correction cut overheating under twin mismatch by 84-85% with no throttling; energy no worse than independent not confirmed in one case (CI -0.17%..+0.31%). Phase 2 lab and API, and Phase 4 calibration tooling added; 73 tests pass.

Phase 4 calibration attempt 1 on the user's RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (driver 610.88; NVML max SM clock 3105 MHz; power limit 125 W). 'nvidia-smi -lgc 1500,1500' was accepted. The warm-up session stopped before measuring with 'PyTorch cannot see a CUDA GPU'; the Administrator window had no venv active, so the likely cause is a different interpreter or a CPU-only PyTorch build (not yet confirmed). No data recorded; an empty session folder was left. Review found the fit normalised clocks by NVML's table maximum (3105 MHz), which this GPU does not sustain: the planned 900-1800 MHz sweep would have sat at s = 0.29-0.58, mostly below s_min = 0.5. Fixed before any data: environment checked before the folder is created (calib check names the cause); s relative to the highest measured compute clock; power fit uses only s >= 0.5 and needs >= 4 clocks; unheld locks and power/thermal limits flagged; calib probe suggests sweep clocks from the sustained clock. 82 tests pass.

Phase 4, RTX 4060 Laptop, first measurement (user-reported console output; data stays on the user's machine until committed): calib probe at default clocks gave sustained SM clock 1860 MHz median (2.1% variation), 51.4 W median board power, 58 C, clock held down by a limit in 100% of steady samples. NVML had reported a 125 W enforced limit when listing devices. The tool version used did not say which limit; low power and temperature point to a power budget set outside the GPU (battery, quiet/balanced mode, or CPU-GPU sharing), not yet confirmed. Tooling now decodes each NVML clock-event reason, logs the enforced power limit per sample, and adds 'calib show' to decode recorded sessions.

Phase 4: calibration moved to the user's desktop PC (laptop readings above stay recorded; the two machines' sessions are never fitted together). Probe at default clocks (user-reported console output): sustained SM clock 2685 MHz median (0.4% variation), board power 250.0 W median / 250.1 W 95th percentile against a reported 250 W limit, 70 C. The driver set no clock-event limit flag, yet power pinned at the limit indicates the clock is set by the power limit. Suggested sweep 1342, 1680, 2017, 2347, 2685 MHz. Tooling: power-at-limit detection, one-GPU-per-calibration guard (fit --device), fan-speed range in the leakage fit with a note when the fan ramps (desktop fans are inside the NVML board-power boundary).
Registered M001-20261026T213241-115dce: GPU calibration measurement (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070) | H: Measurement, not a test: no hypothesis. Values are compared with the registry ranges.

M001 recorded (RTX 5070, desktop PC; 12 sessions: probe, warm-up at 2017 MHz, compute and memory kernels at 1342-2685 MHz locked). Accepted: beta_compute = 0.983 +/- 0.009 (95% CI); beta_memory measured -0.056 +/- 0.079, transferred as 0 (rule R3). Rejected: v_min_ratio (registry linear V-f form ran to its bound: the measured power curve is flat then steep), kappa_leak and p_leak_ref (warm-up held at 53-57 C by the fan, too narrow to identify leakage; unsteady load for several minutes). Model-free: compute-kernel energy per TFLOP lowest at 1657 MHz, 32% below the top clock; memory-kernel energy per GB lowest at the lowest clock, 31% below, with no throughput loss. With registry defaults the simulator gets the size of the saving roughly right but understates savings near the top clock (measured 22% vs 13% at s = 0.88) and overstates them for deep cuts. Indicative only: relative temperature sensitivity of board power 0.09-0.15%/K vs 0.37%/K in the registry. The driver's power-cap flag was set at every locked clock below 2.4 GHz at 35-68% of the power limit, and not at the real 250 W limit: not a limit on this GPU. Report: docs/10_calibration_results.md.

Repository incident: the desktop PC's local results database met the repository's in a git stash conflict; the repository's copy was kept, so the PC's local runs are not in the store. Three of their time-series files were committed without records and are now in results/orphaned/2026-10-26-pc with a forensic note: two are identical to stored E001 S1 seed-0 runs (compute_only, fixed); the third is close to E001 S1 cooling_only (1.8% max difference) and unexplained. The stored E001 runs still reproduce bitwise with current code.

E001C pre-registered (experiments/E001C_calibrated.json, committed before running): E001 design with beta_compute = 0.983 and beta_memory = 0 from M001. Inherited H1-H2 plus HC1 (compute_only saves more vs fixed than in E001 in all 6 scenarios), HC2 (largest change in S5_memory_heavy), HC3 (joint vs independent changes by < 0.5 pp in >= 5 of 6 scenarios). Disclosed: calibration values known, results not; acceptance rules set after the first fit summary; a forensic re-run of 24 seed-0 cells with the rejected first-fit values preceded registration (time series compared, outcomes not examined).

Registered E001C-20261026T213353-ac0b5f: Policy benchmark with measured clock sensitivity (M001: RTX 5070) | H: Inherited from E001 and re-tested: H1: joint uses less energy per successful task than independent in at least 4 of 6 scenarios (paired 95% CI entirely below 0), without more SLO violations or thermal-limit exceedances. H2: every optimising policy uses less energy per successful task than fixed in every scenario. New: HC1: compute_only saves more energy per successful task relative to fixed in E001C than in E001, in all 6 scenarios (seed-paired change in relative saving, 95% CI entirely below 0), because with beta_memory = 0 memory-bound phases lose no throughput when the clock drops. HC2: that change is largest in S5_memory_heavy. HC3: joint's advantage over independent changes by less than 0.5 percentage points (95% CI of the seed-paired change within +/-0.5 pp) in at least 5 of 6 scenarios, because both policies use the same DVFS model.

E001C completed (300 runs, 0 failed; seed-paired against E001). HC1 supported: compute_only's saving vs fixed rose by 4.1-8.7 percentage points in all 6 scenarios (now 20.5-43.4%, E001 14.4-34.8%). HC2 supported: largest change in S5_memory_heavy (-8.67 pp [-9.16, -8.17]). HC3 supported: joint vs independent moved by at most 0.15 pp in all 6 scenarios. Inherited H1 supported (6/6 below zero, 2/6 beyond 1%); H2 energy met, quality guard failed in the same 18 comparisons as E001 (at most +1.4 late tasks per ~2,900). Measured clock sensitivity makes energy-aware clock control look more valuable and leaves the joint-control result unchanged; both still depend on the voltage-frequency and leakage placeholders.
Registered M002-20261026T221416-c4ad2d: Leakage warm-up, attempt 2 (RTX 5070, 2347 MHz, automatic fan) | H: Measurement, not a test: no hypothesis. Values are compared with the registry ranges.

M002 recorded: leakage warm-up attempt 2 on the RTX 5070 (2347 MHz locked, 10 min idle then 15 min load, steady throughput). The fan was under automatic control (0% idle, 27-35% under load) although a fixed fan was intended; the card reached 63 C within two minutes and stayed at 63-64 C; the driver dropped one clock step (2340 -> 2332 MHz) with a ~4 W power step, which made power appear to fall with temperature (-0.22 W/K) under the old +/-15 MHz clock rule. Tooling: leakage samples now kept only at one reported clock step; slopes are always reported (also at constant fan) and recorded by ingest. Slopes: attempt 1 0.177 +/- 0.039 W/K at constant fan (53-57 C, 2.0 GHz, 131 W, 0.135%/K); attempt 2 0.207 +/- 0.014 W/K (61-64 C, 2.33 GHz, 167 W, 0.124%/K, upper bound as the fan rose). Registry at the same points: 0.37 and 0.35%/K. kappa_leak and p_leak_ref remain unidentified (temperature range 3-5 K at constant conditions).

E009 pre-registered (experiments/E009_matched_leakage.json, committed before running): joint vs independent with the simulator's leakage matched to the measured relative slope 0.1346%/K (95% CI 0.105-0.164) at s = 0.747, 55 C; p_leak_ref solved for kappa 0.01/0.02/0.03 (59.4, 29.0, 19.8 W) and for the CI ends at kappa 0.02 (22.2, 35.9 W); registry variant as baseline; M001 clock sensitivity throughout; 6 scenarios x 2 policies x 5 seeds x 6 variants = 360 runs. H1: joint's advantage shrinks vs registry in all 6 scenarios. H2: with matched leakage (kappa 0.02) joint vs independent is within +/-1% (CI) in all 6. H3: H2 holds for every matched variant. H4: independent's chip-seconds over target fall wherever it had any. Disclosed: E002's one-at-a-time leakage results were known and motivated H2.
